title: Restriction compatibility of the proper direct-image coefficient comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $Z,Y$ as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $p:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism and $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ an open immersion. Put $Z_V=Z\times_YV$, let $u:Z_V\hookrightarrow Z$ be the induced open immersion, and let $p_V:Z_V\to V$ be the projection. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module objects over the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings and the derived operations of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a listed coefficient map in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]: a homomorphism of finite commutative $\ell$-primary rings, a finite-extension map $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$, localization $\mathcal O_E\to E$, inclusion $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a continuous map $\mathcal O_E\to A$ to a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, or a finite composite of these. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $F/E$ are finite inside a fixed algebraic closure; topological coefficient rings are condensed, with the finite-subextension convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Write $T_T=(-)_{\Lambda'}$ for derived extension of scalars [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], and $\gamma_{p,M}:T_YRp_*M\to Rp_*T_ZM$ for the unit/pullback-comparison/counit morphism of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]. For $M\in\Dctf(Z,\Lambda)$, bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the canonical open-restriction maps are isomorphisms
$$b_{p,M}:v^*Rp_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{V,*}u^*M,$$
over both $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$. Under these isomorphisms and the pullback coefficient identifications $v^*T_Y\simeq T_Vv^*$ and $u^*T_Z\simeq T_{Z_V}u^*$ of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), one has
$$b_{p,T_ZM}\circ v^*(\gamma_{p,M})=\gamma_{p_V,u^*M}\circ T_V(b_{p,M}).$$
The equality is an equality of morphisms from $T_V(v^*Rp_*M)$ to $Rp_{V,*}T_{Z_V}(u^*M)$ after exactly those identifications. Here the canonical open-restriction map is the usual derived exchange map: insert the unit for $p_V^*\dashv Rp_{V,*}$, use $p_V^*v^*\simeq u^*p^*$, and apply the restricted counit for $p^*\dashv Rp_*$; for an identity square it is the identity under the identity-functor identifications.

proof.text: For the cartesian square defining $Z_V$, the canonical exchange map $b_{p,M}:v^*Rp_*M\to Rp_{V,*}u^*M$ is the proper base-change map. In the finite coefficient case it is an isomorphism by [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite](2); for $\mathcal O_E$ it is an isomorphism by [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral](3); and for $E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it is an isomorphism by [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational](3). Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ covers the $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ stages. The coefficient-change theorem [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf](3) puts $T_ZM$ in $\Dctf(Z,\Lambda')$, so the same argument applies to $b_{p,T_ZM}$; the displayed exchange map is exactly the unit--pullback--counit map specified in the statement by the derived adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

source.place: Independence paragraph: the canonical open-restriction maps.

proof.text: The pullback coefficient identifications $v^*T_Y\simeq T_Vv^*$ and $u^*T_Z\simeq T_{Z_V}u^*$ are the instances for $v$ and $u$ of the natural pullback--coefficient-change isomorphism in [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1). Its composition compatibility identifies both ways of transporting a coefficient-changed object around the cartesian square, so the source and target of the desired equality are literally the displayed objects after these identifications.

Put $q=p_V$, $P=Rp_*M$ and $t=u_\Lambda^*(\epsilon_{p,M})\circ a_P$, where $a:q_\Lambda^*v_\Lambda^*\simeq u_\Lambda^*p_\Lambda^*$. By [lem-sfb-proper-open-coefficient-left-transpose], the left-hand composite, with exactly the two coefficient identifications of step 2, has inverse adjoint transpose $T_{Z_V}(t)\circ c_{q,v_\Lambda^*P}$. Here $c_f$ is the inverse pullback coefficient comparison. The lemma computes the actual specified exchange and coefficient mates, so it applies to the maps in the statement.

By [lem-sfb-proper-open-coefficient-right-transpose], the right-hand composite has the same inverse adjoint transpose $T_{Z_V}(t)\circ c_{q,v_\Lambda^*P}$. Injectivity of the Hom bijection for $q_{\Lambda'}^*\dashv Rq_{*,\Lambda'}$ in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] now proves the required equality. This uses only equality of the transposes; invertibility of the restriction maps was established in step 1.
